name: Dhaka
notes: Buildings, storeys, land use, streets, water, metro lines and stations, and the substations come from OpenStreetMap (© OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL).
Population: 2022 Population and Housing Census (BBS), Dhaka North and South City Corporations, spread over residential floor area.
95 % of buildings have no storey count in OpenStreetMap; theirs is estimated from tagged neighbours.

Service areas are split by nearest grid substation, not from real feeder maps. Only 11 grid substations inside the city are mapped in OpenStreetMap (the real network has many more), so each area is large.
Traction substation positions on the metro are modelled; they are not mapped in OpenStreetMap.
Cars: about 40 per 1,000 people, 2 % of them electric today (approximate).
Demand is scaled so a summer weekday evening peaks near 2,900 MW, roughly the combined peaks reported by DPDC and DESCO, the two Dhaka distribution utilities (approximate).

hospital.name: Dhaka Medical College Hospital
hospital.source: Dhaka Medical College Hospital: 2600 beds (official capacity, approximate; it routinely treats far more patients than beds); location from OpenStreetMap; peak load estimated at 5 kW per bed.
